items.title: George Justin Interview, 1958-06-01
items.q: And every time I'd go down there I used to go by and see him.

ctx.x: And every time I'd go down there I used to go by and see him. But he was one fellow he really learned fast. I mean he's a good musician, he could read anything, he could put in front of him, he could play anything. And on top of that he had such a beautiful tone, beautiful tone. And I would say that he played a different style from anybody else because he didn't play Dixie or he didn't play progressive but his style was more or less on the gut bucket style. And that's what they used to feature a long time ago.
You mentioned records with Lee Collins.

Right. And if you was the type of musician you couldn't play a gut bucket style, you were just lost. And there was another guy down there who was a tremendous musician. I also found out that he wasn't much of a reader either and this was this, what was his name, Handy? Oh John Handy.
